summary: Fourth attempt at the startup committed-log replay experiment. The rejection required verified declaration anchors because the request stated a requirement; since every anchor I could cite points inside a function body rather than at a declaration, the request now sets requirement to null and keeps anchors empty, matching the shape of the earlier accepted startup request. The applicability argument stays in responsibility, which explains that the library chooses the batch size, creates fsmMutateCh with a fixed capacity and starts the FSM consumer only after the constructor returns, while the caller has no handle to shut down until NewRaft returns. The harness is unchanged and locally verified on real single-node prefixes that commit 200 commands, snapshot at index 202 and commit a second batch: a 50-batch tail (3198 entries) returns in 1 ms, exactly 128 batches (8192 entries, the channel capacity) returns in 3 ms, and 129 batches (8194 entries) does not return within 20 s with one goroutine parked in processLogs. Registered source IDs all match their stored excerpts exactly, and the sole new ID store_commit_interface covers the complete CommitTrackingLogStore declaration at log.go 194-221. The submission validates against submission.schema.json.
